text:
**About 300-350 W of panels refills a 1,000 Wh station from empty in one decent sunny day. A 200 W panel does it in about a day and a half.**

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 covers real-world losses from heat, panel angle, and charge controller conversion ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a full recharge in one day |
|---|---|
| 3 (shoulder season, cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer day) | ~270 W |
| 6 (Southwest summer) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). Another guide puts a northern winter (about 2 sun hours) at 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Practical shortcuts:**
- **200 W panel:** about 630 Wh per day at 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency, so roughly 1.5 days to fill ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **100 W panel:** about 3 days.
- **400 W panel:** under a day, about 1,260 Wh per day.
- **Rule of thumb:** divide the battery's Wh by 5 to get the panel watts that fill it in about a day and a half ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Check before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** every station caps how many watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-800 W, and panels beyond the cap add nothing.
- **Voltage window:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within your station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the unit, and wiring panels in series adds voltage.
- **Connector:** panels usually use MC4 connectors, while stations often take XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter.
- **Running loads:** if you use the station while charging, the net recharge is slower.

**If your station accepts 400 W and 12-60 V input,** one option is the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). It lists 45.3 V Voc, includes XT60 and DC adapters, and is $299 ($269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26, per the listing). It's heavy at 18.5 kg, and it's too high-voltage for stations with a low input ceiling, such as 24-28 V. That link is an affiliate link. If your station caps at 200 W, a 200 W panel is the better match.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can check its input limits and suggest a matching panel.
